Government had invited project proposals from all State Governments/ Union Territories for 
consideration under the 'Apparel Parks for Exports' Scheme. Since the inception of 
Scheme in March, 2002, twelve Project Proposals have been sanctioned for setting up 
Apparel Parks at Tronica City and Kanpur (U.P.). Surat (Gujarat), Thiruvanahthapuram

of the Scheme with the basic objective of bringing in urgency in implementation of the 
Scheme. Extensive discussions have been held in the Inter-Ministerial meetings with

Clandestine imports of Chinese raw silk 
1695. SHRI B.K. HARIPRASAD: Will the Minister of TEXTILES be pleased to 
state: 
(a) whether Government have launched futures trading in cocoon and raw silk at the 
National Commodity and Derivative Exchanges to enable the actual users to cover 
price fluctuations; 
(b) whether this move will solely benefit the buyer/end-users of cocoon and raw silk to 
the detriment of producers/sellers who are small marginal farmers; and 
(c) what are reasons of addressing in the basic issue of clandestine imports of Chinese 
raw silk resulting in destablization of domestic market? 
THE MINISTER OF TEXTILES (SHRI SHANKERSINH VAGHELA): 
(a) and (b) Yes, Sir. Futures trading in.raw silk and cocoons has been launched by 
Central Silk Board (CSB) at the platform of National Commodity 
180 

[16 March, 2005] RAJYA SABHA 
and Derivatives Exchange Ltd. (NCDEX) on 20th January, 2005. Futures trading provides, 
an attemate trading avenue for the stake holders like farmers, rubers, weavers and traders 
and helps them through a better price discovery for their produce. It also helps them to 
present the risk associated with price rise and fall and its volatility through hedging. 
Futures trading will not be detrimental to the benefit of producers/sellers who are 
small/marginal Farmers. 
(c) Import of Silk is under Open General License (OGL) since 2001. Silk 
imports into India, mainly from China, have increased substantially after the 
removal of quantitative restrictions on 1.4.2001 and prices have also fallen at the 
same time, leading to market disruption. The matter of putting a curb on clandestine 
imports through the borders falls under the purview of Central Board of Exicse and 
Customs (CBEC) which keeps vigil on the borders of Bangladesh and Nepal to 
curb illicit import into the country.

Need to Establish Special Economic Zone for I.T. Sector at Managalore, 
Karnataka 
SHRI B.K. HARIPRASAD (Karnataka):  Sir, Karnataka has been the cradle 
of IT software and BPO-related ventures for a long time. The State Government 
and assiduously built up the infrastructure and nurtured the industry as a 
precursor to the cyber revolution sweeping the nation. In the process, the State 
has accumulated enough expertise and professional skills in IT majors whose 
facilities are located in Bangalore. 
Keen to replicate its success in promotion of IT-related ventures, the State 
has now identified a few centres—Mangalore among those—for setting up Software 
Technology Parks. Mangalore is emerging as the new hub of software technology 
industry, with 18 companies accounting for an aggregate export turnover of Rs. 
456 crores during 2003-2004. 
Sensing the demand for additional IT hubs, Karnataka has proposed 
establishment of a sector-specific 'Special Economic Zone for IT Sector' at 
Mangalore, in a vast expanse of 508 acres with a capital outlay of Rs. 49.39 
crores. With infrastructure in place, the SEZ would offer 330 acres of fully 
developed and functional workplace for the new entrants. 
[MR. DEPUTY CHAIRMAN in the Chair] 
Sir, I urge the Central Government to accord its administrative approval for the 
project which has been proposed by the Government of Karnataka under the 
guidelines contained in the Foreign Trade Policy-2004-09, announced by the 
Ministry of Commerce and Industry.

Demand to ensure conservation of Dal and Wullar Lakes in Kashmir 
PROF. SAIF-UD-DIN SOZ (JAMMU AND KASHMIR): Sir, I feel extremely sorry to 
say that the Union Ministry of Environment has not still appreciated the urgency 
regarding conservation of Dal and Wullar Lakes in Kashmir. 
The Ministry concerned has not responded to the nation's resolve to 
conserve Dal Lake as a national asset. It was in 1997 that a project was 
approved by the Union Cabinet for an amount of Rs. 297 crores. Some amount 
was released but the project, as a whole, was not implemented. Meanwhile, 
prices have escalated. In 2004, the Standing Committee on Science and 
Technology had made a categorical recommendation for providing 100 per cent 
funding to the Dal conservation from the Government of India. The Ministry doesn't 
seem to have taken any serious notice of that recommendation. 
I urge upon the Ministry of Environment to immediately complete the 
formalities and release funds to t he State Government and monitor 
development and conservation of Dal Lake as a national heritage. 
As for Wullar Lake, the negligence of the Ministry is quite obvious. Wullar is 
Asia's biggest sweet water Lake and long ago it was included in Ramsar 
Convention. It was natural that the Mini stry should fulfil commitments of the 
Ramsar Convention.Wullar today is a vast marsy land. A lake that once 
covered a space of 200 square kilometres has shrunk to just 24 square 
kilometres. I thought, I must raise it to seek support of this august House so 
that the Ministry stirs into taking urgent action.

SHRI B.J. PANDA (Orissa): Sir, my home State Orissa, unfortunately, is one

drbughtprone, like the Kalahandi-Bolangi r-Koraput districts which remain

resulted in severe poverty in the State. The present hon. Chief Minister of the

development.

may be released for Orissa and the State be granted a Special Category Status

Request for categorisation of Scheduled castes into four groups in Andhra 
Pradesh 
SHRI SUDARSHAN AKARAPU (Andhra Pradesh): Mr. Deputy Chairman, 
Sir, the fruit of reservation meant for Scheduled Castes is not reaching in uniform 
and just manner to all the sub-castes in SC category. This is more evident in the 
State of Andhra Pradesh, where unequal distribution of reservation benefit 
amongst different sub-castes had led to deprivation of some sub castes thereby 
defeating the very purpose and spirit of reservation system. In Andhra Pradesh, 
the Scheduled Caste population has been divided into four sub groups, viz, A, B, C, 
& D. The 15 
194 

[16 March, 2005] RAJYA SABHA 
per cent quota of reservation has been distributed amongst different sub castes 
in proportion to their population. This had helped all sub castes under the 
Scheduled Caste category to get benefits in a uniform and just manner and the 
post categorisation had led to marked difference in the lives of all sub castes as 
reservation benefits were evenly dispersed. Recently, on technical grounds, the 
Supreme Court had struck down the Andhra Pradesh Government's order dividing 
59 sub castes of Scheduled Castes into four groups. The Supreme Court had 
opined that Parliament is the competent authority to categorise Scheduled Castes 
into sub groups and that State Legislature have no authority in such matter. 
In view of Supreme Court observation, I request the Government of India to bring 
forward a legislation for suitably amending the Constitution for categorising the 
SC population into four sub groups, viz, A, B, C, & D so that all the sub castes of 
Scheduled Castes get uniform opportunities under reservation.

Need to upgrade Jammu-R.S. Pura-Suchetgrah Road 
SHRI T.S. BAJWA (Jammu and Kashmir): Sir, it may be recalled that a regular 
train service between Jammu and Sialkot existed prior to partition of the country. 
After discontinuation of train services the whole traffic load fell on road between 
Jammu and Suchetgrah. The population of  the area and vehicular traffic has 
increased many-fold. The road between Jammu-Suchetgarh-R.S. Pura is a single 
road and is not able to bear the heavy load due to its dilapidated conditions at 
many places. Vehicle movement is often disrupted due to wear and tear condition 
of an old bridge of about 100 meter length on this road. On an average a vehicle 
passes through every 30 second. Even a small halt at the bridge results in long 
queues of vehicular traffic on both sides, which takes hours to clear. Therefore, 
this highway may be covnerted into a four-lane road and bridges on it should be 
widenend to run traffic smoothly. The train service between Jammu and Srinagar 
may be started to meet the demand and aspirations of the people of the area. The 
development of road between Jammu and Suchetgarh is a necessity for opening 
Jammu-Sialkot bus route. I urge upon Government to pay due attention to this 
aspect and initiate early action for completion of this road. Thank you.

to giving environmental permission for a minor port of Dholera in Gujarat.

sector. The Government of Gujarat has accordingly decided to develop ten places 
for minor ports in private sector. And Dholera port is one of them. The State 
Government has given permission to M/s J.K. White Cement Company for 
developing a minor port through and with the help of the Maritime Board of 
Gujarat. Accordingly, permission and licence was given to M/s Dholera Port 
Limited in September, 1998. This company has submitted a detailed project 
report to the Maritime Board for obtaining clearance. It had also applied for 
environment clearance and for financial closure and Concession Agreement. 
The Gujarat Maritime Board gave approval to the project report of the said 
company on 26th August, 2000. The Gujarat Pollution Control Board also gave a 
No Objection Certificate. The said company has already submitted the necessary 
documents and information on 16th February, 2002, to the Ministry of 
Environment and Forests. Since it is bei ng a minor port, public hearing is not 
necessary. Hence, the company has requ ested the Ministry of Environment 
and Forests, on 27th August, 2002, for giving early clearance so that 
implementation of this project may start immadiately. But, the Ministry of 
Environment decided to have a public hearing on this issue. In compliance with this, 
the Gujarat Pollution Control Board held a public hearing on 29th August, 2003, 
and sent its Report to the Ministry  of Environment and Forests on 12th 
November, 2003. This company has complied with all the requirements of the 
Union Ministry.

*221. SHRI RAJ NATH S INGH:† 
SHRI PROF. SAIF-UD-DIN SOZ:  
Will the Minister of EXTERNAL AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
(a) the details of the proposals for the new rail and bus links between India 
and Pakistan; 
(b) whether Government have examined its viability;

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EXTERNAL

Statement 
New rail and bus links between India and Pakistan 
During the visit of External Affairs Minister, Shri K. Natwar Singh, to 
Pakistan from February 15-17 2005 to Pakistan, agreements were reached to start 
bus services between Srinagar and Muzaffarabad, and between Lahore and 
Amritsar, including to religious places such as Nankana Sahib. Pakistan also 
agreed to work towards early restoration of the Khokrapar-Munabao rail link.

Singh.

provided palpable support to the present process. Security implications of the above 
links have been taken into account and passengers will be allowed to travel on them

Rampant cloning of SIM cards 
*224. SHRIMATI VANGA GEETH A: Will the Minister of 
COMMUNICATIONS AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be pleased to 
state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that the issue of rampant cloning of mobile 
29 

RAJYA SABHA [17 March, 2005] 
SIM cards has raised serious questions over the matter of security not only of 
mobile phone users but also of the country; and 
(b) if so, the steps taken/to be taken by Government in this regard? 
THE MINISTER OF COMMUNICATIONS AND INFORMATION 
TECHNOLOGY (SHRI DAYANIDHIMARAN): (a) and (b) As far as Global 
System for Mobile (GSM) networks in the country are concerned, in which 
Subscriber Identification Module (SIM) cards are used in mobile phones, no 
instance of cloning of SIM cards has been reported in the country so far. 
Moreover, no complaint of cloning of SIM cards in GSM network has been 
referred by any Service Provider either with the Department of 
Telecommunications or with Telecom Regulatory Authority of India. 
However, cloning of Code Division Multiplex Access (CDMA) mobile 
have come to the notice. The CDMA phones not have a SIM card. 
The Cloning of SIM cards may cause  concerns to security of the 
country. However, the same can be avoided by making chances of cloning 
extremely rare by having latest authentication algorithms and timely detecting 
cases in proactive manner using Fraud Management System. 
In this regard, GSM Association has already circulated security 
algorithms to its members. The network operators are required to deploy and 
activate the same in all SIM cards and their network. Some of the Operators 
have already deployed such algorithms in their network.

Settling of unskilled workers in United Kingdom 
*227. SHRI TARIQ ANWAR: Will the Minister of EXTERNAL 
AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that unskilled settlers from developing countries will 
now not be permitted to stay in United Kingdom; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; and 
(c) whether the Indian unskilled workers will also be affected? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EXTERNAL 
AFFAIRS (SHRI E. AHAMED):  (a) to (c) Yes, Sir. All non-EU citizens, 
including Indian citizens, in lower skilled categories will be affected once the 5-
year strategy for immigration and asylum system titled "Controlling our borders: 
making migration work for Britain", meant to enforce strict controls to root out 
abuse and illegal immigration; strengthen the UK's borders; and increase 
removals, is implemented by the British Government. The details of the new 
visa rules of the British Government are given in the Statement. 
32 

[17 March, 2005] RAJYA SABHA 
Statement 
New visa rules of the British Government 
Key measures in the strategy include introduction of a points system for 
selection of those wanting to enter UK for work or study. Points will be allocated 
according to qualifications, work experience, income and other relevant factors 
like local availability of UK or EU workforce. There will be no automatic right 
to stay in the UK for lower skilled workers. They will have to leave when 
their visas expire. 
2. Four tiers — highly skilled, skilled, low skilled and student/ 
specialist — have been created, as follows: 
"Tier 1 (Highly Skilled): The most highly skilled—including doctors, 
engineers, finance experts and IT specialists — will be able to come to the UK 
without a job offer. This will be on the basis of their qualifications from 
graduate level upward, work experience and current salary, with additional 
points for those with skills, the UK needs the most. This will ensure that highly 
skilled individuals can enter the UK to look for woFk or self-employment 
opportunities. Investors and entrepreneurs will continue to be welcome to the UK 
and will score enough points on the basis of the level of their investment or the 
jobs they create". 
'Tier 2 (Skilled): Others, with skills at NVQ level 3 (A-level equivalent) and 
above, will be able to come if they have a job offer in a shortage area, and 
where an employer cannot find the skills they require within the UK or EU. This 
will ensure that UK employers have access to the skills and experience they 
need. Tier 2 workers would include nurses, teachers and administrators." 
"Tier 3 (Low Skilled): In the light of the additional labour now 
available from the new EU cduntires, the UK will phase out over time current 
quota based schemes in the agricultural, food processing and hospitality 
sectors. The UK will take this forward during a review of the sectors 
concerned. Where additional n eeds are identified in future, the UK will 
introduce small tightly managed quota based schemes for specific shortage areas 
and for fixed periods only, with guarantees that migrants will leave at the end 
their stay." 
"Tier 4 (Students and Specialists): This tier will bring together students 
and a range of schemes where there is no significant issue of 
33 

RAJYA SABHA [17 March, 2005] 
competition with the domestic labour force, including visiting workers 
representing overseas Governments or international companies based in the UK. 
Skilled workers in these categories can choose to come in Tiers 1 or 2 if they 
wish to make the UK their home. The UK will retain the Working 
Holidaymaker scheme for young Commonwealth nationals but tighten the 
criteria."

charges for last three years, year-wise and category-wise;

THE MINISTER OF COMMUNICATIONS AND INFORMATION 
TECHNOLOGY (SHRI DAYANIDHIMARAN): (a) to (f) Telecom Regulatory 
Authority of India (TRAI) has reduced the Access Deficit Charges (ADC) in 
rupees per minute applicable for various types of calls i.e. ADC rates -v/de its 
IUC Regulation dated 6.1.2005, which has been implemented w.e.f. 1.2.2005. 
The Overall ADC amount for the fixed line operators has not been 
reduced. All the fixed line operators have been provided ADC funds of the 
same order specified under the earlier regime of 29th October, 2003 which was

given the flexibility to offer tariffs subject to certain regulatory principles. 
Further Bharat Sanchar Nigam Limi ted (BSNL) has informed that 
reduction in ADC has no relation with the rationalization of call charges of

*237. SHRIMATI N.P. DURGA: Will the Minister of SCIENCE AND 
TECHNOLOGY be pleased, to state: 
(a) what measures his Ministry are taking to give single-window 
clearance to all the biotechnology related proposals;

five years; year-wise; and

43 

RAJYA SABHA [17 March, 2005] 
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF SCIENCE AND 
TECHNOLOGY (SHRI KAPIL SIBAL): (a) to (c) The Government of India has 
established a well-conceived regulatory framework for approval of biotech 
products with independent appraisal and approval bodies for compliance of 
different Acts and Rules to ensure the high levels of environmental safety 
including human and animal health. The expertise and authority for different 
components of the regulatory framework for biotech products are with the 
different departments of the Government. For harmonization of the regulatory 
approval procedure, Government has set-up two committees one for the 
recombinant pharma sector under the chairmanship of Dr. R. A. Mashelkar, DG 
CSIR and another for the Agri- Biotech sector under Dr. M.S.Swaminathan. 
The committees' recommendations have resulted in making the regulatory 
procedures simpler, more science based and efficient. An inter-ministerial board 
has been proposed for considering long-term reforms in the regulatory system. 
According to the surv ey conducted by Biot ech Consortium India 
Limited (BCIL), Biospectrum and Association of Biotechnology Led 
Enterprises (ABLE), the total expor t of biopharmaceutical, bioindustrial, 
bioservices, bioagri, bioinformatics and biosupplier products in the years 2001 -
2002,2002-2003 and 2003-2004 was to the tune of Rs. 875 crores, Rs. 1029 crores 
and Rs. 1817 crores respectively. The export of biotech products has seen a 25-
30 per cent growth in last five years. The Government of India (GOI) has 
given enough attention to the innovative biotech sector with an impetus for the 
development and promotion of this sector. It has brought the biotech sector at 
par with IT sector in terms of incentives. With this biotech innovative sector, 
which is highly knowledge intensive enjoys a number of benefits as on date in 
terms of finance and in terms of support from the GOI. For export promotion 
GOI has given EOU status to all units located in Biotech Parks as notified in the 
Foreign Trade Policy.

Disposal of radioactive wastes 
1700. SHRI KRIPAL PARMAR: 
SHRI B.J. PANDA: 
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that management and disposal of long-life 
radioactive wastes, has been a technical and political problem the world over; 
(b) whether it is fact that Energy Research Group of Reliance in their 
report has recommended certain solutions for safe storage of nuclear waste; and 
(c) if so, the details thereof with action plan of Government to address the 
issue? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE PRIME MINISTER OFFICE (SHRI 
PRITHVIRAJ CHAVAN): (a) The manageme nt and disposal of long life 
radioactive wastes has been an important issue world over. Safe technological 
solutions do exist and several countries have taken steps in this direction. Disposal 
of such waste in deep geological formations is an accepted option. Many 
countries including India have similar approach. International programmes 
supported by agencies like International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) on public 
awareness have been going on to educate the public and mitigate their 
apprehensions. 
(b) The Energy Research Group of Reliance Industries Ltd., have 
prepared a review report which briefl y covers aspects of radioactive waste 
disposal. The report concludes that th ere is an international consensus on 
disposal of long-lived radioactive waste in deep geological formations on land. 
(c) The work on development of process and technology for 
management of radioactive waste was started by the Department of Atomic Energy 
about four decades ago along with the development of other components of 
Indian Nuclear Energy Programme. A three step strategy has been adopted in 
India for the management of long lived radioactive waste, which comprises 
of:— 
(i)   conversion of radioactive waste into stable, inert, solid waste form 
such as borosilicate glass, 
53 

RAJYA SABHA [17 March, 2005] 
(ii)   interim storage for a period of 30-50 years, and 
(iii)   final disposal in deep underground geological repository in the long 
term. 
The Indian programme in the area of radioactive waste management for 
long-lived waste is fully geared up to meet the country's needs. 
Titanium deposit left by Tsunami on Tamil Nadu beaches 
1701. SHRI EKANATH K. THAKUR: Will the PRIME MINISTER be 
pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that the December 26 Tsunami has left behind 
millions of tonnes of titanium ore on the beaches of Tamil Nadu; 
(b) whether it is also a fact that known global resources of the ore are in 
the range of 285 million tonnes and tita nium is among the most sought after 
metals in the world; and 
(c) if so, in what manner Government propose to use the newly added 
titanium on the because of Tamil Nadu? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE PRIME MINISTER'S OFFICE 
(SHRI PRITHVIRAJ CHAVAN): (a) Along the coastal sretches of Tamil 
Nadu, the deposition of heavy minerals due to tsunami is patchy, inconsistent 
and with a maximum thickness of 30-40 cm. Among the existing deposits, 
llmenite and Rutile are titanium bearing minerals. In some instances the 
tsunami waves have destroyed the existing concentrations in dunes and 
deposited them inland, thereby relocating the existing deposits. Thus there is no 
substantial enhancement of heavy mineral deposits in Tamil Nadu. 
(b) Yes, Sir. Titanium is the metal of future and India has an abundant 
resource of titanium minerals. The resources of titanium ore (ilmenite) in India 
alone is 374 million tonnes as on 1.1.2004 based on the studies by Atomic 
Minerals Directorate for Exploration & Research (AMD).

Statement 
Common Charter of Telecom Services, 2005 
1. All Service Providers acknowledge the rights of citizens to have a free 
choice in selecting their Service Providers and agree to promote 
their services in the best spirit of competition and traditions of 
service to. consumers; 
2. All Service Providers agree to promote the consumers' right to 
education, choice, representation and redress; 
3. All Service Providers assure that the privacy of their subscribers (not 
affecting the national security) shall be scrupulously guarded; 
4. All Service Providers assure that their subscribers shall be entitled 
to interact with them, either personally or through their authorised 
representatives; 
5. For information and education of subscribers, all Service Providers 
agree to inform their subscribers of the broad range of services 
offered, the individual plans available to them at any given point of 
time, the tariff rates applicable to each of these, their validity, terms 
and conditions, payment policies, the billing processes and 
procedures and the structure within the organization where 
information and clarification on consumer redress systems for 
complaints and billing disputes will be available with all their 
relevant contact numbers; 
6. All Service Providers agree to arrange human interface with 
responsible company executives whose name and identity are 
61 

RAJYA SABHA [17 March, 2005] 
made known during the process of disputes resolution in addition to 
arrangements like Customer Care Service through Call Centres; 
7. All Service Providers agree to periodically inform their subscribers 
on the reverse of their bills, their consumer grievance redress process 
with respect to fault complaints and billing disputes. They also 
agree to resolve the disputes as pe r the guidelines of TRAI issued 
from time to time; 
8. All Service Providers agree to provide an applicant basic telephone 
connection within 7 days of registration, subject to technical 
feasibility and the mobile connection immediately subject to 
compliance of all required formalities by the subscriber; 
9. All Service Providers agree to repair the faults within 24 hours of 
receipt of complaint from a subs criber wherever technically 
feasible; 
10. All Service Providers agree to ensure shifting of telephone 
connection within 3 working days within the same exchange, 5 
working days for intra city and 30 working days for inter city 
exchanges and closure (disconnection) of telephone connection within 
3 days on receipt of a letter of request from the subscriber. An 
authenticated copy of the last telephone bill shall accompany the letter 
of request; 
11. All Service Providers agree to provide in their bills related call and 
tariff details, payment procedures and list of points at which payments 
can be made by subscribers; 
12. All Service Providers agree to regi ster complaints in all areas of 
their service immediately, if delivered in person or by e-mail and 
within 24 hours on receipt of the complaint by post; 
13. All Service Providers shall render service without discrimination to 
every citizen as per his eligibility defined below and who 
undertakes to pay all charges and deposits; 
"For the purpose of this clause, a citizen shall be defined as an 
individual above the age of 18 or an institution, NGO or 
business/service organization enga ged in any activity which is 
permissible under the laws of the land" 
62 

[17 March, 2005] RAJYA SABHA 
14. All Service Providers agree to provide information on Directory 
Services and book complaints on toll free number for registering 
complaints; 
15. All Service Providers agree to provide their subscribers satisfactory 
connectivity to their services and interconnectivity to the extent of 
their respective legal obligation under the relevant interconnection 
agreement and to ensure the subscribers do not suffer on account of 
poor service; 
16. All Service Providers agree to levy reconnection charges as per the 
TTO or waive the same on their own discretion; 
17. All Service Providers agree to allow emergency services like police, 
fire and ambulance for a period of 15 days during which incoming 
facility is allowed, if technically feasible, even after the telephone 
connection is suspended. 
18. The subscribers agree to clear all dues within the specified time; 
19. All Service Providers agree to achieve the minimum benchmarks 
prescribed by TRAI with respect to the quality of service and also 
commit themselves to improve upon the standards of service at different 
points of time; 
20. Mutual courtesy and respect are the hallmarks of any durable 
relationship between the Service providers and subscribers and both 
agree to abide by these principles. 
Though this charter is non-justiceable, Service Providers agree to strive 
to adhere all the points contained in this charter and to make every effort to 
abide by the charter.

India's stand after Tsunami 
1736. DR. AKHILESH DAS: Will the Minister of EXTERNAL 
AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
(a) the steps being taken by Government in the aftermath of the 
Tsunami disaster in the South Asian region to establish its position as a 
benefactor in the region and to prevent outside powers to get foothold in India's 
backyard; 
(b) the expenditure involved; and 
89 

RAJYA SABHA [17 March, 2005] 
(c) the powers involved in the process and the nature and extent of the aid 
given by each outside power to each Tsunami affected country? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EXTERNAL 
AFFAIRS (SHRI E. AHAMMED): (a) In respect of Sri Lanka, a massive relief 
effort was launched in which India deployed an air detachment of 10 aircraft 
for three weeks and sent about 15 naval ship-loads of supplies, fifteen medical 
teams a mobile field hospital (140 men) that was airlifted, specialist doctors, a 
45-bed hospital ship (INS Jamuna), 10 teams of naval divers and a 81-member 
composite Army disaster management team. Indian ships and aircraft were the 
first to arrive in Sri Lanka. This contingent provided immediate emergency 
assistance; re-commissioned Galle harbour; provided emergency medical services 
to tens of thousands of Sri Lankans; and in the initial confusion among 
administrative authorities functioned as temporary command centres. Ten 
truckloads of supplies sent by Cll were handed over to the Ramakrishna Mission 
at Point Pedro in Northern Sri Lanka for distribution among affected people in 
that area. 
Subsequently, the Sri Lankan Government has commenced the 
"Rebuilding the Nation Programme." In response to Sri Lankan requests in this 
regard, RITES has conducted a preliminary technical assessment of damaged 
railway links and a team from the Ministry of Health visited Sri Lanka on Feb. 
23—28 for assessing Sri Lankan requirements in the health sector. The 
Government of India earlier dispatched 5 Bailey Bridges to Sri Lanka which have 
been put to use in restoring crucial road links. Tamil speaking psychiatrists 
have also been deployed to help survivors overcome emotional trauma and a 
consignment of homeoepathic medicines has been supplied. 
In respect of Maldives, India deployed an air detachment of 4 aircraft and 2 
ships at a time for about three weeks. These assets were used for search and 
rescue, damage assessment and transport of supplies and communication with 
remote atolls. Naval personnel went ashore and helped provide essential services, 
assisted in sanitation operations and provided medical relief. They also repaired 
communication facilities. They also played a crucial role in coordination and 
controlling relief efforts in the early stages. 
(b) Prime Minister has said that Rs. 100 crore will be made available for 
relief to Sri Lanka and Rs. 5 crore for relief to Maldives. 
90 

[17 March, 2005] RAJYA SABHA 
(c) TheTsunami disaster in Sri Lanka and other Indian Ocean rim 
countries attracted a very high degree of international attention and evoked an 
enormous outpouring of compassion and international assistance to the affected 
countries, including Sri Lanka and Maldives. 
Exact details of the assistance to Sr i Lanka are not readily available as 
assistance was channeled through a number of sources including UN agencies 
and NGOs. However, as per available information, it is known that the United 
States deployed about 700-800 US Marines on the island of Sri Lanka for relief 
operations; Pakistan deployed two ships, three aircraft, 50 marines a field 
hospital, 180 man army engineering team, and a shipload of earthmoving and 
transport equipment; Bangladesh deployed one ship, a diving team and two 
aircraft; UK deployed two ships and helicopters; Russia deployed aircraft; and 
disaster management teams were deployed by Canada and France. In addition to 
the above, it is known that Canada, Germany, UK, China and mu ltilateral 
agencies have announced a number of financial measures such as debt-relief 
for Sri Lanka. A number of countries have also made financial donations and 
pledges to assist in the reconstruction of Sri Lanka. 
Precise details of assistance to Mald ives are not readily available as 
assistance was routed thro ugh a number of channels including UN agencies 
and NGOs. As per available information two Pakistani ships that were already in 
Male when the Tsunami struck were deployed on emergency relief operation; 
Bangladesh deployed a patrol vessel and a helicopter; and France deployed a 
naval vessel. A number of countries have made financial donations and pledges 
to assist in the reconstruction of the Maldives.

.missing defence personnel, it was inter-alia agreed that: 
(i) Immediate notification would be provided to the respective High 
Commissions through the Foreign Ministries of arrested 
Pakistani/Indian nationals; 
(ii) Consular access would be provided within three months of 
apprehension; 
(iii) Repatriation would be done immediately after completion of 
sentence and nationality verification; 
(iv) A mechanism would be introduced for early repatriation, without 
sentencing of inadvertent crossers; 
(v) A similar mechanism would be established for early release, without 
sentencing of those under 16 apprehended by either side. 
India announced Visa on arrival at Wagah Border for Pakistani 
nationals above 65 years, children below 16 years, and pre-vetted groups; and 
grant of Student Visas to Pakistani nationals on a case-by-case basis. 
The Foreign Secretary Level talks initiated the second round of the 
Composite Dialogue. The following programme was chalked out to continue the 
talks further: 
It was decided that technical meeti ngs including the Joint Study Group 
on Trade and Economic Cooperation headed by the Commerce Secretaries, 
Indian Coast Guards and Pakistan Maritime Security Agency, Pakistan Rangers 
and Border Secrurity Force of India, Expert level dialogue on Nuclear and 
Conventional CBMs, technical level meeting on bus service between/through 
Amritsar and Lahore, meeting between the Narcotics Control Authorities 
would be held between January and June 2005. 
It was agreed that the meeting on the other six subjects under the 
Composite Dialogue, i.e. Siachen, Wullar Barrage/Tulbul Navigation Project, 
Sir Creek, Terrorism & Drug Trafficking, Economic & Commercial Cooperation 
and Promotion of Friendly Exchanges in Various Fields would be held on 
mutually agreed dates between April and June 2005.

Passports under Tatkal Scheme 
1750. SHRI K.B. KRISHNAMURTHY: Will the Minister of 
EXTERNAL AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
(a) the number of passport applicati ons received, on an average, per 
day at Bangalore Passport Office under Tatkal Scheme; 
(b) the procedure for obtaining passports under Tatkal Scheme; 
(c) if so, the average number of days taken to issue passports under 
Tatkal Scheme; 
(d) whether Government are aware that  at Bangalore Passport Office, 
there is no separate counter for Tatkal Scheme and after applying under 
general category, it has to be converted under Tatkal Scheme; and 
(e) the steps proposed to be taken to ensure opening of separate 
counters and expedite the process under Tatkal Scheme at Bangalore 
Passport Office? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EXTERNAL 
AFFAIRS (SHRI E. AHAMMED): (a) Pa ssport office Bangalore receives, 
50-60 applications daily under Tatkal Scheme. 
(b) An applicant in need of urgent travel abroad can apply for issue of 
Passport under Tatkal Scheme. The ap plicant has to produce a verification 
certificate from an authoris ed person on the prescribed proforma, regarding 
his/her eligibility for issue of passport. Tatkal fee of Rs. 1500/- is charged in 
case the Passport is required within 10  days and Rs. 100/- thereafter. The 
Passport validity, however, is limited to one year only, pending police 
verification. 
121 

RAJYA SABHA [17 March, 2005] 
(c)In cases of acute urgency and subject to completion of the required 
documentation, the passport can be issued on the same day and in not so 
emergent cases, within 3—7  days. 
(d)and (e) Passport Office Bangalore is being instructed to open a 
separate counter for Tatkal applications. 
Authentication of Certificates 
1751. SHRI T.T.V. DHINAKARAN: Win the Minister of EXTERNAL 
AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
(a)whether it is a fact that Indian going to certain countries for job 
opportunities to have to get their certificates authenticated by Government of 
India; 
(b)if so, the details thereof; 
(c)whether Government also have such stipulation for people coming from 
these countries to India; and 
(d)if so, the details thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EXTERNAL 
AFFAIRS (SHRI E. AHAMMED): (a) Yes,Sir. 
(b)Several countries require authentication of educational degrees and 
other official documents like marriage certificates of Indian nationals seeking 
employment there, by the Government of India. 
(c) Yes, Sir. 
(d)Foreign documents are accepted in India only after similar 
authentication by concerned foreign governments and duly attested by our 
diplomatic missions resident in those countries. 
Indian peacekeeping forces under UN aegis 
1752. SHRI VIJAY J. DARDA: W ill the Minister of EXTERNAL 
AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it Is a fact that Indi a has on the request of the United 
Nations, agreed to increase the strength of its peacekeeping force under UN 
aegis to 8,000 troops; 
122 

[17 March, 2005] RAJYA SABHA 
(b) if so, presently in which countries our peacekeeping troops are 
deployed; 
(c) the number of casualities, if any, Indian troops suffered during the 
last five years when serving as UNO peacekeeping forces in different parts of 
the world; and 
(d) whether our troops are adequately compensated for this hazardous nature 
of duties? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EXTERNAL 
AFFAIRS (SHRI RAO INDERJIT SINGH): (a) and (b) At present, a total of ' 5636 
troop from the Indian Army and Air Force are deployed in the United Nations 
Organization Mission in the Democratic Republic of Congo (MONUC), the 
United Nations Mission in Ethiopia and Eritrea (UNMEE) and the United 
Nations Interim Force in Lebanon (UNIF IL). Besides, 123 Armed Forces 
personnel are deployed as staff Officers and Military Observers in various U.N. 
Peacekeeping Missions. Inidia has committed to provide additional troops to the 
UN Mission anticipated in Sudan. If the Mission is established and India is 
requested to provide troops, the total strength of Indian troops in UN 
Peacekeeping Operations would increase to around 8,000. 
(c) Indian Armed Forces troops have suffered two casualties in the last 
five years, while serving in UN Peacekeepings Missions. The first casualty 
was sustaind in an encounter against rebels in Sierra Leone in 2000 and the 
other in the Democratic Republic of Congo, in a land mine explosion in 2002. 
(d) the troops are adequately compensated for the hazardous nature of duty.

Achievement of SAARC 
1754. SHRI MURLI DEORA: Will the Minister of EXTERNAL AFFAIRS 
be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government have opted out of the SAARC summit; 
(b) if so, the reasons therefor; 
(c) whether countries of South Asia do not have a common security 
doctrine and perceive the SAARC as a vehicle to countervail India; 
(d) if so, the Government's reaction thereon and the steps taken to do this 
manoeuvering; and 
(e) how for the purpose of setting up this organisation has been 
achieved? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EXTERNAL 
AFFAIRS (SHRI E. AHAMMED): (a) No, Sir. 
(b) Does not arise. 
(c) Member States of SAARC do not have a common security doctrine. Some 
member countries have tended on occa sion to perceive SAARC as a vehicle 
primarily to countervail India. 
124 

[17 March, 2005] RAJYA SABHA 
(d) and (e) Government supports the objectives of SAARC which was 
established to promote economic, social and cultural cooperation as well as 
mutual understanding and strengthen collective self .reliance among the peoples of 
South Asia. Since its inception in 1985, SAARC has contributed to greater 
understanding, accommodation and information flow, which has led, first to a 
preferential trading arrangement (SAPTA), and subsequently to the signing of 
a Framework Agreement for free trade (SAFTA), currently under negotiation 
with a view to bringing it into force from January 1,2006. The Social Charter and 
conventions signed on issues such as trade, f ood security, terrorism, narcotic 
drugs and psychotropic substances, preventing and combating trafficking in 
women and children for prostitution, and promotion of child welfare in South Asia 
offer instruments for Member States to formulate programmes and implement joint 
strategies in these key areas. People-to-people contact has also increased with 
NGOs and civil society playing a dynami c and incremental role in nurturing 
cooperation and activating ideas on economic, cultural, social and 
development objectives. 
Meeting of Nepalese King with Indian Envoy 
1755. SHRI AMAR SINGH: Will the Minister of EXTERNAL AFFAIRS 
be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that King Gyanendra of Nepal, who has recently seized 
direct control of Nepal, has met envoy s of key nations including India and 
U.S.; 
(b) if so, the details thereof and the nature of talk he had with our envoy 
in Kathmandu; 
(c) whether Government have decided to stop military aid to Nepal after 
the recent events; and 
(d) if so, the details thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EXTERNAL 
AFFAIRS (SHRI E. AHAMMED): (a) Yes, Sir. 
(b) The Indian Ambassador in Nepal had an audience with King 
Gyanendra on February 9,2005. During the meeting, the Ambasador urged a return 
to democratic processes in Nepal at the earliest. He emphasized 
125 

RAJYA SABHA [17 March, 2005] 
the importance of bringing the political party leaders into a broad national 
consensus to enable Nepal to overcome the political and economic challenges 
confronting it. In this context, he called for immediate release of political 
leaders and lifting of restrictions on their constitutional rights and removal of 
censorship on media. 
(c) and (d) Following the dismissal of the multi-party Government and 
imposition of emergency in Nepal on February 1,2005, the issue of military 
supplies to Nepal has been under continuous review taking into acc ount the 
evolving situation in that country. In view of the current disturbed conditions in 
Nepal, no military supplies by Government of India have been delivered 
since February 1.

People Below Poverty Line 
†1799. SHRI ISAM SINGH: Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to 
state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that 41.4 crore people in India are living under the 
Below Poverty Line as per a report of the World Bank; and 
(b) if so, the action plan with the Government to redress this problem 
alongwith details thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PLANNING (SHRI 
M.V. RAJASEKHARAN): (a) No, Sir. A ccording to the lastest World Bank 
Report (World Developments Indicators, 2004), during 1999-2000, 34.7 
percentage of the population in India were living on less than $1.08 a day at 1993 
international prices. It implies that 34.7 crore people of India were living under 
the Below Poverty Line according to International Poverty Line of$1 a day during 
1999-2000. (India's population during 1999-2000 was 1001 million). 
(b) The Government has adopted a three pronged strategy for reducing poverty 
(i) acceleration of economic growth with a focus on sectors which 
† Original notice of the question was received in Hindi. 
168 

[17 March, 2005] RAJYA SABHA 
are employment intensive; (ii) human and social development through 
provision of basic minimum services ; and (iii) targeted anti poverty 
programmes. 
In prder to take care of basic needs of India's poor at the village level, an 
initiative in the form of Prime Minister's Gramodaya Yojana (PMGY) was 
launched. The PMGY envisages Additional Central Assistance for selected 
basic minimum services in order to focus on certain priority areas of the 
Government. These include primary health, primary education, rural shelter, 
drinking water, rural electrification and nutrition. 
In addition, with effect from June, 1997 the Public Distribution System in 
India was streamlined by issuing special cards to families Below Poverty Line 
(BPL) and selling food grains under PDS to them at specially subsidised 
prices which was about 50% of the economic costs. Under the new scheme, viz., 
the Targeted Public Distribution System (TPDS) each poor family is entitled to 
35 kgs. to foodgrains. 
In order to make the TPDS more focused and targeted towards the very 
poor category, the "Antyodaya Anna Yojana" provides 35 kgs. of foodgrains 
to the poorest of the poor families at a highly subsidized rate of Rs. 2 per kg., for 
wheat and Rs. 3 per kg., for rice. In the recent budget presented on 28-02-05 it 
was announced that the coverage of Antyodaya Anna Yojana will be increased 
from 2.0 crore (BPL) families to 2.5 crore families in 2005.

Standards of weather forcasting 
1804. SHRI PRAMOD MAHAJAN: Will the Minister of SCIENCE 
AND TECHNOLOGY be pleased to state: 
(a) whether weather forecasting in our country is upto Global 
Standards; and 
(b) if not, the steps taken to make it upto Global Standards? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF SCIENCE AND 
TECHNOLOGY (SHRI KAPIL SIBAL): (a) and (b) The short range forecast 
issued by Indian Meteorological Department (IMD) is on par with other 
countries of the world. 
IMD has been issuing forecast of seasonal rainfall during southwest 
monsoon, using models indigenously developed for the purpose. These models 
have not been able to. forecast some of the droughts in recent years due to the 
complex nature of the monsoon. Since no other issues seasonal forecasts in 
respect of the Southwest monsoon, there are no global standards to go by. 
However, our equipment and mathematical models need upgradation to reduce 
the margin of error since no science can accurately make prediction of seasonal 
rainfall. Besides, rainfall forecasting requires synergy between land based, space 
and ocean based observations for which a group has been set up to prepare new 
models, again to reduce the margin of error. 
The medium range forecast is crucial for agricultural operations. To meet 
this requirement Government has started a National Centre for Medium Range 
Weather Forecasting (NCMRWF) at New Delhi. This centre is functioning under 
Department of Science & Technology (DST) since

THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF SCIENCE AND

Stem-cell research 
1807. SHRI RAJEEVSHUKLA: W ill the Minister of SCIENCE AND 
TECHNOLOGY be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government feel a need for regulating stem-cell research in 
India; 
(b) if so, the details of any legislation being considered in this behalf; and 
(c) if not, the reasons therefor? 
175 

RAJYA SABHA [17 March, 2005] 
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF SCIENCE AND 
TECHNOLOGY (SHRI KAPIL SIBAL): (a ) to (c) National Biothethics 
Committee set up by the Department of Bio-Technology (DBT) with the 
approval of Hon'ble Minister of Science and Technology in its sixth meeting 
recommended promotion of stem cell research in the country in view of its vast 
potential and its clinical use. There are no special legal or ethical problems in 
respect of stem cells, derived from adults, bone marrows or foetal cord blood. 
However, in respect to embryonic stem  cells the Government does not allow 
generation of embryos for the sole purpose of obtaining stem cells. Only surplus 
or spare of supernumerary embryos can be used with the permission of 
couples from registrered Assisted Reproductive Technique (ART) clinics. 
The Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR), Ministry of Health and 
Family Welfare was requested by the Drugs Controller General of India 
(DCGI) to prepare appropriate guidelines to help in regulation of stem cell research 
and its application. Accordingly, a drafting committee provided brief guidelines for 
regulatory aspect of stem cell research to DCGI. These draft guidelines have been 
put on the website of the ICMR. The guidelines suggested constituting a 
multidisciplinary National Apex Committee (NAC) to monitor stem cell research 
activities in the country. It was also emphasized that newer technology should be 
thoroughly examined before approving any research. It was further suggested that 
this committee should examine all proposals involving stem cells of any source. 
Centres involved in stem cell research should be registered with the committee. 
Currently in the absence of a National Committee, an Expert Committee has 
been constituted to monitor and review stem cell research activities under ICMR. 
The issues regarding legislation and ethical issues involved in stem cell research 
are being discussed by a joint working group of ICMR and DBT.

1827. SHRI B. J. PANDA: Will the Minister of SHIPPING , ROAD 
TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that Government are working out a new Maritime Policy; 
(b) if so, the salient features thereof; and 
198 

[17 March, 2005] RAJYA SABHA 
(c) what is the action plan of Govern ment to involve private sector in 
Maritime sector to tap its potential? 
THE MINISTER OF SHIPPING, ROAD TRANSPORT AND 
HIGHWAYS (SHRI T. R. BAALU): (a) and (b) Yes, Sir. The draft policy has 
identified port productivity which lags behind in comparison to globally 
acceptable benchmarks, inadequate draught availability in entrance/ approach 
channels of Indian ports, inadequate hinterland connectivity, declining tonnage 
share of Indian flag vessels, low modal share of Inland Water Transport (IWT) in 
transportation of cargo, declining profile of shipbuilding/ship-repair industry and 
level of private investment including foreign direct investment amongst major areas 
of concern and seeks to lay down the vision and strategy for addressing these 
concerns. The following objectives are sought to be realized under the 
policy:— 
(i) Holistic development of maritime transport systems through a 
coordinated plan and strategies for development of port 
infrastructure, improvement in shipping, backward integration of the

†1839. SHRI RAM JETHMALANI: 
SHRI RAJ MOHINDER SINGH MAJITHA 
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that the target of poverty alleviation from the country can 
not be achieved merely by investing money in Plan implementation; 
(b) if so, the reaction of Government thereto;

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PLANNING (SHRI M.V. 
RAJASEKHARAN): (a) and (b) Yes, Sir. It is a fact that the target of poverty alleviation

provision of basic minimum services; and (iii) targeted anti-poverty programmes.

RAJYA SABHA [17 March, 2005] 
With effect from June, 1997 the Public Distribution System (PDS) in India 
was streamlined by issuing special cards to families Below Poverty Line (BPL) 
and selling foodgrains under PDS to them at specially subsidised prices which was 
about 50% of the eco nomic costs. Under the new scheme, viz., the Targeted 
Public Distribution System (TPDS) each poor family is entitled to 35 Kgs. of 
foodgrains. 
In order to make the TPDS more focused and targeted towards the very 
poor category, the "Antyodaya Anna Yojana" provides 35 kgs of foodgrains to 
the poorest of the poor families at a highly subsidized rate of Rs. 2 per kg., for 
wheat and Rs. 3 per kg., for rice. In the recent budget presented on 28-02-05 it 
was announced that the coverage of Antyodaya Anna Yojana will be increased 
from 2.0 crore (BPL) families to 2.5 crore families in 2005. 
Rural Areas 
The major rural poverty alleviation programmes which are in operation are 
Swaranjayati Gram Swarozar Yojana (SGSY), Sampoorna Grameen Rozgar 
Yojana (SGRY) and Rural Housing-Indira Awaas Yojana (IAY),  National 
Food for Work Programme 
• The objective of the SGSY is to bring the assisted poor families 
(Swarozgaries) above the poverty line by organizing them into Self 
Help Groups (SHGS) through the process of social mobilization, 
their training and capacity building and provision of income generating 
assets through a mix of Bank credit and Government subsidy. 
• The primary objective of the SGRY scheme is to provide additional wage 
employment in all rural areas and thereby provide food security and improve 
nutritional levels. The secondary obj ective is the creation of durable 
community, social and economic assets and infrastructural development in 
rural areas. The SGRY is open to all rural poor who are in need wage 
employment and desired to do manual and unskilled work in and around the 
village/habitat. 
• The Indira Awaas Yojana (IAY) is the major scheme for construction of 
houses to be given to the poor, free of cost. It has an additional 
component, namely, conversion of unserviceable kutcha houses to semi 
pucca houses. 
214 

[17 March, 2005] RAJYA SABHA 
• The National Food for Work Programme has the objective to provide 
additional resources to 150 most backward districts of the country 
so that generation of supplementary wage employment and provision 
of food security through creation of need based economic, social 
and community assets in these districts is further intensified. 
Foodgrains are provided to the St ates free of cost. Works are taken 
up under the programme in accordance with the Fi ve Year Perspective 
Plan. The collector is responsible for preparation of the Perspective 
Plan and programme implementation. 
Urban Areas 
• : The Poverty Alleviation Programme which seeks to provide gainful 
employment to the urban unemployed or under-employed poor through 
encouraging the setting up of self-employment ventures or provision of wage 
employment is Swarna Jayanti Shahari Rozgar Yojana (SJSRY). The programme 
targets the urban poor, defined as those living Below the Poverty Line, as defined 
from time to time. This programme relies on creation of suitable community 
structures and delivery of inputs is through the medium of urban local bodies and 
such community structure. It is funded on at 75.25 basis between Centre and the States. 
The Programme is applicable to all urban towns in India. The Programme is 
implemented on a whole town basis with special emphasis on urban poor clusters. 
The implementing Ministries have systems of monitoring through mechanisms 
such as periodic progress reports, inspection by Government officials, Areas-Officers' scheme, 
Performance Review Committees etc. In addition, regular impact assessment studies and 
evaluations of specific schemes are also undertaken. Further, the release of funds is subject 
to receipt of Utilisation Certificates and Audit Reports. Based on programme evaluation and 
review, the schemes have been restructured and redesigned from time to time.

Outcome to the meeting of Sports Ministers 
1844. SHRI LALIT SURI: Will the Minister of YOUTH AFFAIRSAND 
SPORTS be pleased to state: 
(a) the topics discussed in the conference of Sports Ministers held in Delhi in 
February last; 
(b) the decisions arrived at; and 
(c) the steps so far taken by Government and the those proposed to be taken to 
implement them? 
THE MINISTER OF YOUTH AFFAIRS AND SPORTS (SHRI SUNIL DUTT): (a) 
The Major issues discussed in the Conference related to subjects of transferring 'Sports' to the 
Concurrent List of the Constitution; formulation of State Youth & Sports Policies; 
implementation issues in respect of new schemes, strengthening and monitoring and delivery 
mechanism of various programmes of the Ministry etc. 
(b) The general view on some of the key issues, which emerged out of the 
discussions were: 
1. The annual budgetary allocation for the Union Ministry of Youth Affairs and 
Sports needs to be substantially enhanced. 
2. Review of the decision to transfer of Centrally Sponsored Scheme for Sports 
Infrastructure, as it would adversely affect the future growth of sports 
infrastructure in the country. The committed liabilities of Rs. 160 crores 
should be provided for during the next 2 to 3 years. 
3. Further consultation was required in the respective States on the issue of bringing 
the subject of 'Sports' in the Concurrent List of the Constitution Individual 
State Governments shall take a view on the subject and send written 
communication in this regard.

RAJYA SABHA [17 March, 2005] 
4. Autonomous premier organizations like Sports Authority of India and Nehru 
Yuva Kendra Sangathan (NYKS) should be made more effective, responsible and 
accountable and their field formations should have closer interaction with State 
agencies.. The financial as well as administrative structure of these 
organizations may also be strengthened and expanded further. 
5. Need for formulation and adoption of State Youth and Sports policies by all the 
States and Union Territories. 
6. Plan of Action for Celebration of 2005 as International Year of Physical 
Education and Sports be implemented. 
7. Need for greater stress on physical education in institutions by introducing it 
as part of the curriculum. 
8. Revision of the Scheme of State Sports Academy so as to utilize the existing 
sports infrastructure for broad basing sports. 
9. Need for providing mass participation in physical fitness by involving Panchayati 
Raj Institutions, NYKS, etc. 
 
10. Early formulation of Scheme for setting up National and State Youth Centres 
as envisaged under the Tenth Five Year Plan. 
11. The State Ministers Conference should be made an annual feature.

THE MINISTER OF PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS (SHRI MANI 
SHANKAR AIYAR): Sir, I beg to move: 
That the Bill to repeal the Parel In vestments and Trading Private Limited 
and Domestic Gas Private Limited (Taking Over of Management) Act,

[17 March, 2005] RAJYA SABHA 
With your leave, Mr. Deputy Chairman, might I seek your indulgence to explain the 
background to this Bill? M/s Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited, a Government of India 
Undertaking was formed after merging four companies at different points in time, 
namely, ESSO, Lube India Undertakings, Caltex and Kosangas Company. HPCL has 
an all-India presence in the LPG business. 
Two companies, namely, M/s Parel Investments and Trading Company Limited (PITCL) 
(formerly known as Parel Investments and M/s Trading Private Limited) and Domestic 
Gas Private Limited (DGPL) were concessionaires of Caltex, appointed as distributors for 
the sale of Caltex's packed LPG for southern and eastern India. The Government of India took 
over the management of PITCL and DGPL, and, pending acquisition of their LPG 
business, HPCL were appointed as custodian through the Parel Investments and Trading 
Private Limited and Domestic Gas Private Limited (Taking Over of Management) Act, 
1979. 
Sir, the Goculdas Group of Companies, the common promoter of ' these two 
companies, filed writ petitions in the Delhi High Court in 1979 in respect of these companies. 
The Court granted interim relief to the petitioners and ordered that the non-LPG business 
of these companies shall not be taken over by the Government/HPCL. Shri R.M. Goculdas, 
the authorized representative of the Goculdas Group of Companies, offered an out-of-court 
settlement to the Government in 1985. It was felt that a negotiated out-of-court settlement, 
would end long drawn out litigation. Pending finalization of the settlement, the writ petitions 
were disposed of by the Delhi High*Court in December, 1996 with liberty to the parties to 
apply for their revival, if need be. However, the settlement could not be finalized. 
In February, 2000, Shri Ashok Chandra, former Secretary, Ministry of Petroleum and 
Natural Gas, was appointed to hear all the interested parties and give his 
recommendations. 
On the basis of these recommendations, an out-of-court compromise settlement was 
negotiated between the Goculdas Group of Companies, HPCL and the Ministry of 
Petroleum and Natural Gas. It envisaged taking over the LPG business of PITCL and 
DGPL only at a nominal amout of Rs. 10,000/-, handing back the management relatingto 
non-LPG business of the Goculdas Group of Companies, and not raising any dispute in future 
251 

RAJYA SABHA [17 March, 2005] 
with regard to taking over the management/assets and liabilities of their LPG business. 
The title of the LPG business of the two companies was required to Devested in HPCL 
in order to regularize HPCL's investments in modernizing and expanding their LPG business. 
The acquisition of their LPG business would enable HPCL to maintain the bottling, 
transporting, marketing and distribution of LPG 
In accordance with the decision, the conveyancing of LPG business and related 
assets of PITCL and DGPL in favour of the Government of India/HPCL has since been 
effected through deeds of assignment on 2.4.2004. 
Under the deeds of assignment, all th e assets relating to LPG business, 
namely, lease holds, land building, gas cylinders, bottling and filling facilities, tank lorries, 
LPG stock, bank balances, books of accounts, registers have been acquired and transferred, 
subsequent to management take over in 1979. In addition, only liabilities arising out of deposits 
collected from customers for.LPG cylinders,.gratuity to employees, current liabilities relating to 
sundry creditors and wages of employees have been assumed by the Government/HPCL. 
The remaining liabilities continue to be with the respective companies. 
The Apt of 1979 had displaced the Board of Directors of the two companies and 
had empowered HPCL to perform all functions of the Board of Directors. Under the deeds, the 
management of the said two companies, shall be relinquished in favour of the respective two 
companies, except in relation to the LPG related business which has been acquired. 
An amount of Rs. 10,000/-has been paid for the assignment of the LPG business 
to each of the said two companies. 
Under the deeds, the officers and workers employed in the LPG business of 
PITCL and DGPL shall be absorbed on the rolls of HPCL. 
Their employment shall continue on the same terms and conditions as were 
applicable prior to the acquisition and until revised by HPCL. 
As the process of conveyancing is completed, it is now proposed to repeal the Parel 
Investments and Trading Private Limited and Domestic Gas Private Limited (Taking Overof 
Management) Act, 1979. The present Bill aims at this.

STATEMENT BY MINISTER 
Launching of an unemployment benefit scheme for workers from 
the new financial year 
THE MINISTER OF LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT (SHRI K. 
CHANDRA SEKHAR RAO): Sir, I am happy to announce to the House that in 
pursuance of the Common Minimum Progr amme of the UPA Government and 
under the guidance of the UPA Chairperson, Shrimati Sonia Gandhi, and the hon. 
Prime Minister, Dr. Manmohan Singh, the Ministry of Labour and Employment has 
taken a momentous decision to implement a highly labour-friendly Scheme 
called the Rajiv Gandhi Shramik Kalyan Yojana. This Scheme shall be 
implemented by the Employees State Insurance Corporation, a statutory 
organization under the Ministry of Labour and Employment. 
We often come across situations  where industrial units and other 
establishments are closed down for a variety of reasons, beyond the control of the 
workers. During such periods of unemployment, and till they are able to find 
alternative employment, the economic and social condition of 
254 

[17 March, 2005] RAJYA SABHA 
the workers and their families becomes highly vulnerable. The absence of a safety 
net to deal with such situations leads to frustration and impoverishment of the 
workers. 
Insured persons covered by the Employees State Insurance 
Corporation, and losing employment after 1st April, 2005, on account of closure 
of factories or establishments, retrenchment, or permanent invalidity arising out of 
non-employment injury, shall be covered under this scheme. The insured workers 
who lose employment after having contributed to the ESI scheme for five or more 
years shall be entitled to an Unemployment Allowance in cash, which would be 
equivalent to about 50 per cent, of their wages, for a maximum of six months. 
In addition, the insured persons in receipt of Unemployment Allowance and their 
families shall also be eligible to receive medical care, as available in the ESI 
dispensaries and the ESI Hospitals. 
This scheme which will come into forc e from 1st April, 2005 will provide 
the much needed social security cover for about eight million employees who 
are insured with the Employees State Insurance Corporation. The medical 
benefit will extend to 30 million family members of the insured workers. 
The Employees State Insurance Corporation proposes to meet the 
expenditure of the Scheme out of its existing resources without levying any 
additional burden either on the employ ees or on the employers. Rs. 300 
crores are being provided for in the Rules under the ESI Act for this purpose. 
Hon. Deputy Chairman, Sir, this is for the first time that an 
unemployment-related benefit scheme is being launched in the country for our 
brethren workers, and I am sure that  all categories of workers and their 
employers in the country would welcome this important welfare measure.
